newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Lara strikes form for West Indies.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Lara strikes form for West Indies.

text.p: A resurgent West Indies celebrated Brian Lara's return to form with a six-wicket victory over Pakistan in their limited overs World Series match on Friday.
Lara ended a dismal run of low scores by hitting 48 as West Indies maintained their recent improvement in a tense encounter at the Gabba.
In reply to Pakistan's total of 197 all out in 49.5 overs, West Indies scored 198 for four with 11 balls to spare.
Carl Hooper, batting one place below Lara at number five in the order, scored an unbeaten 54, his 20th in limited overs internationals, to guide his side to victory.
Hooper was joined by Jimmy Adams in an unbroken fifth-wicket partnership worth 74 runs. Adams contributed a valuable 33 not out.
Lara, who has endured a miserable test series against Australia, scoring a paltry seven runs in his last four innings, finally found some touch and timing.
But the world record holder for the highest score in test cricket almost found himself back in the pavilion with another failure to his name after a tentative start.
The West Indies vice-captain was extremely fortunate to survive a huge appeal for leg before wicket after playing back in his crease to a yorker from fast bowler Mohammad Zahid.
After losing their first two matches in the triangular competition, West Indies have won two in succession.
West Indies, Pakistan and hosts Australia all have four points from four games at the half-way stage of the qualifying round.
Coming back into the attack for a second spell of extreme pace, Zahid finally accounted for Lara when the left-hander offered a catch off the bottom edge to wicketkeeper Moin Khan.
Sent into bat by West Indies captain Courtney Walsh, Pakistan stumbled to 47 for four on a lively pitch before Ijaz Ahmed steadied their nerves with a patient 59 off 122 balls.
